CHROMIUM: drm/virtio: Fix cache entry creation race. virtio_gpu_cmd_get_capset would check for the existence of an entry under lock. If it was not found, it would unlock and call virtio_gpu_cmd_get_capset to create a new entry. The new entry would be added it to the list without checking if it was added by another task during the period where the lock was not held resulting in duplicate entries. Compounding this issue, virtio_gpu_cmd_capset_cb would stop iterating after find the first matching entry. Multiple callbacks would modify the first entry, but any subsequent entries and their associated waiters would eventually timeout since they don't become valid, also wasting memory along the way. Signed-off-by: David Riley <davidriley@chromium.org> BUG=chromium:923211 TEST=repeatedly startvm and check glxinfo -B | grep Device Change-Id: Ie2603e80891fb73bd05b64621447a3c7c93c5609 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1629038 Commit-Ready: David Riley <davidriley@chromium.org> Tested-by: David Riley <davidriley@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Gurchetan Singh <gurchetansingh@chromium.org>

Revert "gdbm: disable building of berkdb compat library" This reverts commit 2c607444d90c31f8140e4cf637ea21caddcc0e27. It turns out we do care about building gdbm with the berkdb compat library, or at least maybe we should. The factory tests have been using gdbm with python since commit 5d666cb4108c6cafa6174637025c8ee1276e06b1 ("Add Python support for gdbm (used by factory tests)."). Somewhere along the line, upstream python ebuilds have been enforcing an RDEPEND=(gdbm ? sys-libs/gdbm[berkdb]) - that is, the gdbm must be built with USE=berkd if python is built with USE=gdbm. Apparently the chromiumos-overlay version of the python 2.7 ebuild forked before this was changed upstream and still do not include this requirement. Let's unblock building gdbm[berkdb] to remove one difference with the upstream python ebuild. Signed-off-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> BUG=chromium:736313 TEST=emerge-grunt gdbm Change-Id: I7aef1d41090e8f2412edc02aa1055149a3d03445 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/580216 Commit-Ready: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Tested-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Chris McDonald <cjmcdonald@chromium.org>

init: chromeos_startup: Avoid clobber when TPM ownership is unknown To determine if TPM is owned, we try to read a file and that ends up sending a tpmc command to TPM. In case the command fails to execute, the function is_tpm_owned was returning "false", which would trigger the device clobber if install attributes is present. Here we change this, to consider that TPM is owned if the command fails, thus avoiding the device clobber in such case. The only risk this has is the case when TPM is cleared, install attributes is present and TPM command to determine if owned fails. In that case we end up with some dead data on disk. This is much less problematic than having the device clobber by mistake. BUG=chromium:929695 TEST=None Change-Id: I17598c560c115cb6fd2d2c6edce4b14f88ad9c37 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1626095 Commit-Ready: Igor <igorcov@chromium.org> Tested-by: Igor <igorcov@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Igor <igorcov@chromium.org>

shill: openvpn: Re-use routing information when re-connecting An existing issue with shill's native OpenVPN implementation is that connectivity is lost after a suspend-resume is performed, due to missing routes in the VPN's per-device table. Since these routes should not change, OpenVPN will simply assume that the VPN client maintains the routing information provided during the initial connection. This change causes the OpenVPNDriver to preserve existing routing information between reconnections. BUG=chromium:843407 TEST=-Performed sleep-resume and saw that routes came up as expected. -`test_that $BOARD network_VPNConnect.openvpn` passes. shill: drop ad-hoc support Ad-hoc networks are * used at a negligible rate; * known to be broken, to some extent (e.g., we disconnect/reconnect during every scan); * not supported by all vendors; and * not tested in our automated lab. Let's drop support for them. For the moment, I leave the 'Mode' Service property intact, even though it only serves to advertise a single option now ('managed'). We stop reporting metrics -- will follow up with removal of the histogram in Chrome. Notable behaviors: * we now filter out any unsupported mode when reporting endpoints (WiFi::BSSAddedTask()), which prevents ad-hoc networks from showing up in our Service list; this gets tested now in WiFiMainTest.ScanResults * we *don't* explicitly purge old stored Profile entries which could still have WiFi.Mode==adhoc; these will get loaded, but they won't do anything if no endpoint is matched to them BUG=chromium:931442 TEST=unit tests TEST=manual: set up IBSS network -- does not appear in Service list Change-Id: Ib4db4f54d171e767a8af8440f45ac23573563b70 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1626253 Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org>
